messages:
dani: FYI customer ACME (INC-4592) reporting lots of 5xx + timeouts hitting our hosted inference API. They see p95/p99 spikes and a bunch of gateway timeouts. asking for an ETA and repro steps they used.

ops-bot: ALERT: hosted.request_queue_depth{pool=\"hosted\"} > 900 for 7m, action: paging.#ops

lee_oncall: I’m on it, paging SRE. Initial guess: continuous-batcher backlog causing tail-latency timeouts / early rejects.

emma_support: Customer says they sent a sustained stream: ~2k req/min for 8m, many small prompts (~10-20 tokens) across concurrent clients. They got intermittent 502/504 and then 5xx bursts.

mike_prodeng: Sounds like queue depth + batching thresholds. When queue depth climbs, we start early-evictions and fallbacks to heavy path which increases tail latency. Could be kvcache pulls causing head-of-line stalls.

lee_oncall: Can someone paste quick metrics? I’m pulling logs.

karen_sre: metrics: 
```
# prometheus quick
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=request_queue_depth%7Bpool%3D%5C%22hosted%5C%22%7D" | jq .data.result
# sample: value ~ 920
```

karen_sre: batching backlog length: continuous_batcher.pending_batches=42, avg_batch_wait_ms=1820, p99_batch_wait_ms=7230

lee_oncall: logs (gateway):
```
[2026-03-17T08:12:01Z] gateway request_id=acme-0a1b2c path=/v1/generate status=504 queue_depth=918 srv_lat_ms=14000
[2026-03-17T08:12:02Z] gateway request_id=acme-0a1b2d path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_err=worker_timeout kv_fetch_ms=4600
[2026-03-17T08:12:05Z] gateway request_id=acme-0a1b3f path=/v1/generate status=500 reason=batcher_deferred_eviction
```

emma_support: Customer supplied a short repro: run 5 concurrent clients each sending 400 requests/min small prompts over 10 minutes. They included correlation ids in header X-ACME-ID.

dani: Escalation: customer is using hosted tier for production traffic; they want mitigation now or they’ll move to dedicated. We should prioritize.

lee_oncall: Immediate mitigations I’m doing: 1) temporary raise request_queue_depth soft-limit for hosted pool from 1000 -> 1400 (safe short window), 2) enable per-tenant rate cap bypass to route ACME to warm pool, 3) scale up continuous-batcher replicas by +2.

mike_prodeng: Approved. Also pushing a quick config to lower max_batch_wait_ms from 10s -> 3s for high-queue signals, so batches flush faster (reduces head-of-line). Risk: small throughput loss.

karen_sre: After changes: queue_depth dropped to ~300 within 90s, p99 latency improved from 14s -> 2.7s for sampled traces. No further 5xx reported in next 4m.

ops-bot: NOTE: Incident severity set to sev2 (customer-facing outage). Ticket INC-4592 updated with mitigation info and temp SLA credit offer.

emma_support: Customer confirmed reduced errors. They asked for root cause and durable fix.

lee_oncall: Root cause hypothesis: rapid tenant traffic spike + small prompt distribution pushed continuous-batcher into long waits due to KV cache-backed shard fetches and queue-depth limit triggered early-eviction path. Combined effect = high tail latency and gateway 5xx.

mike_prodeng: Long-term fixes proposed: 1) tenant-adaptive batching thresholds (dynamic max_batch_wait based on queue depth), 2) per-tenant warm pools (fast path) for sticky customers, 3) improve kvcache lazy-load to avoid 4-5s cold fetches on hot shards.

dani: Action items:
- lee_oncall: runbook writeup + postmortem (due 72h)
- mike_prodeng: design ticket for adaptive batching (JIRA INF-7123)
- platform: schedule tenant warm-pool pilot (ops request)

lee_oncall: Adding runbook note: when request_queue_depth > 800 AND p99_batch_wait_ms > 5s -> escalate to SRE, consider temporary soft-limit bump and scale continuous-batcher.

karen_sre: Reproducer command we used internally:
```
# simple repro from perf lab
for i in {1..5}; do seq 400 | xargs -n1 -P20 curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-ACME-ID: repro-$i" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://hosted-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done
```

emma_support: Marking INC-4592 as mitigation in place. Customer will monitor 24h and open follow-up if they see recurrence.

dani: Thanks all. Please add any extra notes to the postmortem and include cost impact estimate for temporary scaling (ops billing).

mike_prodeng: Noted. I’ll also add tests to the eval harness to simulate small-prompt high-rps patterns so we catch regressions.

lee_oncall: Closing the active pager. Will ping when postmortem draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
